evidence.reference_title: Scientific understanding and clinical management of Dupuytren disease.
evidence.snippet: Dupuytren disease (DD) is a fibroproliferative disorder of unknown etiology that often results in shortening and thickening of the palmar fascia, leading to permanent and irreversible flexion contracture of the digits.

nodes.description: Progressive flexion contracture of the fingers caused by fibrotic thickening of the palmar fascia; the defining clinical feature of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Wnt signaling and Dupuytren's disease.
evidence.snippet: Dupuytren's disease is a benign fibromatosis of the hands and fingers that leads to flexion contractures.

nodes.description: Activated myofibroblasts deposit excessive extracellular matrix with a characteristic increase in type III collagen relative to type I. As cellular nodules mature into relatively acellular collagen-rich cords, the contracted matrix becomes a fixed structural deformity along the digital rays.

nodes.description: Repetitive microtrauma, local ischemia, and oxidative stress in the palmar aponeurosis initiate a dysregulated wound-healing response. nodes.description: Palmar fibroblasts transdifferentiate into alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive myofibroblasts under the influence of TGF-beta. These contractile cells populate the proliferative nodules and generate the active contractile force that, together with collagen deposition, draws the digits into flexion.

evidence.snippet: Dupuytren's disease (DD) is a fibroproliferative disorder that manifests as an abnormal growth of myofibroblasts, causing nodule formation and contractures and affecting digit function.

nodes.description: Locally produced TGF-beta and other growth factors, together with immune cell infiltration, amplify the fibrotic response and drive resident fibroblasts toward an activated, contractile phenotype. Aberrant Wnt/beta-catenin signaling is a hallmark molecular feature of Dupuytren tissue, and genome-wide association studies additionally implicate developmental Hedgehog and Notch signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Wnt signaling and Dupuytren's disease.
evidence.snippet: The fact that six of these nine loci harbor genes encoding proteins in the Wnt-signaling pathway suggests that aberrations in this pathway are key to the process of fibromatosis in Dupuytren's disease.

evidence.snippet: The presence of immune cells and related phenomena in DD-affected tissue suggests that DD is possibly immune-related.

nodes.description: Low-dose external beam radiotherapy applied to early-stage nodular disease in an attempt to slow progression before fixed contractures develop; the supporting evidence base remains limited.

nodes.description: Open surgical excision of the diseased palmar fascia, the traditional treatment for advanced contractures, offering durable correction at the cost of greater morbidity and recovery time.
